answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a small, time-locked deposit of quartz-backed credit before it may transact, with the stake slashed if peers flag fraud. Newcomers start behind a velvet rope: limited volume until their history earns trust, so one operator cannot cheaply spin up thousands of sock puppets. Reputation must then wander with the agent across services instead of resetting, making each fake identity expensive to grow and cheap to lose.
